svg.title: Innate immune response to bacterial infection
svg.desc: Bacteria entering a tissue set off two arms of innate immunity. Macrophages recognise them through Toll-like receptors and release cytokines and chemokines, which bring neutrophils out of the blood. Complement is activated on the bacteria and coats them with C3b. The two arms meet when phagocytes engulf the opsonised bacteria, killing them with the respiratory burst and trapping others in neutrophil extracellular traps.
